extracted.intended_audience: comedy writers, humor writers, stand-up comedians, and readers interested in comedy craft
extracted.subtask_description: A short blog recommendation endorsing Tina Fey's Bossypants as essential reading for people who write or study comedy, with implicit criteria about what makes a comedy writer credible and worth reading. Useful for readers seeking resources on comedy craft and examples of comedic voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation: Bossypants is a must read for comedy/humor writers
rubrics_metrics.description: "Bossypants," by the always funny, Tina Fey is a must read if you’re into comedy writing, humor writing or you just want to be entertained by a sharp-witted, super-intelligent and smokin’ hot comedy writer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author advises readers to "do yourself a favor and visit the N.Y. Times review before you buy, but pick up the book. You’ll enjoy every page." This frames the book as both instructive for craft and enjoyable as entertainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career impact and innovation as credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: "What makes Tina Fey so special? Well, she was not only the best thing to happen to Saturday Night Live since the days of Dan Akroyd, Bill Murray, John Belushi, etc., She is the only one to leave SNL and start her own show, '30-Rock.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post uses notable career achievements (SNL success; creating 30 Rock) as a signal that an author has earned authority to teach or exemplify comedy writing; career innovation is presented as evidence of creative leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versatility: excelling as both writer and performer
rubrics_metrics.description: "Where she stands toe-to-toe with a practically all-male cast and not only kills it as a writer, but also has us captivated with her genuineness as an actress."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points to the value of being both a strong writer and an authentic performer; authenticity/genuineness onstage and in performance is highlighted as a key quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productivity and real-world experience
rubrics_metrics.description: "while in the midst of writing 30-Rock, doing guest appearances on SNL, raising her child and a multitude of other endeavors, she’s also found the time to write books."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portrays the ability to produce work under heavy real-world commitments (writing TV, performing, parenting) as enhancing the author's credibility and the practical usefulness of her insights for working comedians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enjoyability/entertainment value as an evaluative criterion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond technical instruction, the post emphasizes that a worthwhile comedy book should be entertaining to read; readability and humor in the prose itself are part of its value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim: the book 'breaks the mystery of comedy'
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Book that Breaks the Mystery of Comedy" (site heading/claim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit rubric: a useful comedy-writing resource should demystify craft — offering clear, accessible insights into how comedy works rather than obscuring it.
